The following tutorials illustrate the funtionality of *trimes*.

# Getting Started
This [tutorial](getting_started.qmd) introduces the basic data structure of *trimes*. It covers basic concepts like (re-)sampling, interpolation and slicing. 

# Time Series Comparison
This [tutorial](time_series_comparison.qmd) covers the comparison between time series signals and the calculation of metrics. Starting from simple subtraction, metrics like root mean squared error for upper and lower boundaries (envelope) are calculated. Finally, step response data is analyzed. The tutorial also illustrates some helper functions for plotting (e.g. fill between two time series).

# Time Series Generation
This [tutorial](time_series_generation.qmd) covers the generation of time series signals. It is shown how to create linear interpolated signals and periodic signals (superimposing several frequencies).

# Signal Processing
This [tutorial](signal_processing.qmd) covers the application of signal processing methods to time series data. It includes examples of filtering, Fourier analysis, and other common signal processing techniques.

# Analytic Signals
This [tutorial](analytic_signals.qmd) covers test signals that carry their own analytical ground truth (amplitude, frequency and phase as callables): the `AnalyticSignal` object from `trimes.analytic` and its `ground_truth` / `phasor` / `rocof` output, ready-made generators from `trimes.synchrophasor` (steady state, modulation, frequency ramp, magnitude / phase step) and phase-continuous concatenation. This is the basis for benchmarking phasor, frequency and ROCOF estimators.

# Synchrophasor Compliance Testing
This [tutorial](synchrophasor_tests.qmd) builds the IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1:2018 test matrix (`trimes.synchrophasor.conditions`), runs an estimator against it and produces a pass / fail compliance table with `trimes.synchrophasor.metrics` (TVE / FE / RFE, `summary`, `compliance`). It also shows parameter sweeps, three-phase tests and `concat_segments` scenarios.
